skills.name: ai-ml
skills.summary: Routes work on trained-model systems to the right sub-skill: LLM apps (prompting, RAG/retrieval, agents and tool use, evals and LLM judges, guardrails, fine-tuning) or classical ML projects (framing, baselines, model choice, missing data, deployment, retraining). - Use even when no ML jargon is used: the chatbot makes things up or ignores instructions, should we fine-tune, how do I test prompt changes, the agent loops or calls the wrong tool, how do we know it still works in production, is this model good enough to ship, which model for this tabular or image data, accuracy dropped after launch, when should we retrain. Not for generic data wrangling or plotting, SDK/API syntax, or MCP server implementation.

skills.name: architecture
skills.summary: Routes software architecture work to the right sub-skill; use when choosing system topology or code organization, service boundaries, domain models, component structure, C4 diagrams, coupling or cohesion, or architecture rules for CI. Not for single-file placement or routine refactors. - Use even when the word architecture is absent: how should I structure or organize this project, how should this repo be split into modules, two services share a database, draw an overview of how the system fits together, make CI enforce layering rules, model this domain. Not for single-file placement or routine refactors.

skills.name: architecture-pattern-advisor
skills.summary: Guides repository architecture choices for topology or code organization; use when selecting or restructuring either, not for generic project setup.

skills.name: c4-modeling
skills.summary: Drafts C4 system diagrams in Mermaid at Context, Container, Component, Landscape, Dynamic, or Deployment level; use when documenting a system as C4, not Code.
skills.compatibility: No dependencies — Mermaid renders natively on GitHub, GitLab, and most Markdown tools, and in VS Code with a Mermaid extension. Optionally C4-PlantUML for publication-grade output when PlantUML (Java) or a Kroki server is available.

skills.name: communication-analysis
skills.summary: Analyzes or rewrites feedback and messages using Schulz von Thun's four-sides model and Rogers-style active listening; use for diagnosis or rewrites, not therapy.

skills.name: coupling-cohesion
skills.summary: Assesses existing code for module cohesion and LCOM, codebase-wide coupling metrics and zones, or the balance of one dependency (Khononov).
skills.compatibility: The bundled scripts are stdlib-only Python 3.8+. LCOM analyzes Python (precise, via AST), R, and Bash (heuristic); the coupling and balance checks are language-agnostic. Dependency-graph extraction uses whatever tool fits the ecosystem (examples in the Mode B file for Python, JS/TS, Java, .NET, Go).

skills.name: ddd
skills.summary: Applies Domain-Driven Design to boundaries, context mapping, tactical patterns, aggregates, value objects, events, and event sourcing; use for DDD design or review.

skills.name: documentation
skills.summary: Guides writing or revising technical docs for a named reader — README, tutorial, how-to, API reference, docstrings, runbook, package docs, or vignettes.

skills.name: fitness-functions
skills.summary: Designs and implements architecture fitness functions — automated CI checks that fail the build when a characteristic such as modularity, layering, coupling, security, or resilience erodes.

skills.name: html-artifacts
skills.summary: Produces a self-contained HTML file for deliverables the reader will keep, share, or manipulate; not for ordinary answers.

skills.name: hypertrophy-training
skills.summary: Guides experienced trainees in hypertrophy programming, auto-regulation, and plateau diagnosis.

skills.name: improve-codebase
skills.summary: Scans a codebase for architectural deepening opportunities and guides a round-by-round review of candidates using a visual report with before-and-after diagrams.
skills.compatibility: Requires git and a browser to view the HTML report. Writes only to the OS temp directory, plus the repo's GLOSSARY.md and ADRs when the user agrees.

skills.name: llm-application-engineering
skills.summary: Engineers LLM applications for output quality, retrieval, fine-tuning, evals, agents, guardrails, and monitoring; use when building or debugging an app on an LLM.

skills.name: logical-component-design
skills.summary: Decomposes a NEW system or feature into named logical components; not for measuring an existing decomposition.

skills.name: microservices-design
skills.summary: Guides microservice interaction design and review — boundaries, coupling, communication style, contract versioning, sagas, and resiliency patterns from Newman's *Building Microservices*.

skills.name: ml-project-lifecycle
skills.summary: Guides a classical ML project from framing and baselines through model choice, missing data, deployment, and retraining; use when training on supplied data, not building an LLM app.

skills.name: natural-planning
skills.summary: Plans one multi-step project with GTD's Natural Planning Model (purpose, outcome, brainstorm, organize, next actions).

skills.name: oss-scouting
skills.summary: Scouts a third-party open-source repository for a small, suitable issue, then prepares a reproduction, root-cause analysis, fix diff, tests, and a submission checklist in a local folder.
skills.compatibility: Requires git and read-only GitHub access through the GitHub MCP tools or the GitHub CLI (`gh`). Running a candidate's reproduction needs that project's own toolchain.

skills.name: poc-spec-loop
skills.summary: Guides a greenfield R, Python, or Bash PoC to production readiness through an interactive specification and a per-task TDD loop.
skills.compatibility: Requires jq, one loop runner CLI (claude, codex, or opencode), and the forge CLI (gh, or az with the azure-devops extension) on PATH, a single GitHub or Azure DevOps Services remote, plus the language toolchain in references/toolchains.md (uv, R/Rscript, or bats/shellcheck/shfmt).

skills.name: problem-first-explanation
skills.summary: Structures explanations of tools, methods, concepts, rules, and proposals by leading with the concrete problem.

skills.name: pypet-snippets
skills.summary: Curates shell-command snippets with the pypet CLI, including creating, finding, editing, running, and aliasing snippets or proposing one from recurring shell commands.
skills.compatibility: Requires pypet-cli 0.9 on PATH (upstream archived Aug 2026, final v0.9.0).

skills.name: refactoring
skills.summary: Finds where refactoring is worth starting in an unfamiliar codebase by ranking files by git churn (hotspots) and explaining the ranking.

skills.name: release-pr
skills.summary: Prepares a release pull request for an R or Python package, then tags and publishes the release after merge.
skills.compatibility: Requires git plus the forge's CLI — `gh` or the GitHub MCP tools (GitHub), `az` with the azure-devops extension (Azure Repos), or `glab` (GitLab); other hosts fall back to git only. R packages need Rscript with usethis and devtools; Python packages need uv. `scripts/release_state.py` is stdlib-only (tomllib on Python 3.11+, regex fallback below).

skills.name: repo-status
skills.summary: Generates a standup or status update from recent development activity, including yesterday's work, today's plan, and blockers, using rough notes or connected-tool activity.

skills.name: stakeholder-update
skills.summary: Drafts a weekly update, executive summary, escalation, or launch announcement for readers outside the working group.

skills.name: tldr
skills.summary: Compresses long material into the facts needed to decide or act, including recent messages and named files, PRs, documents, or threads.

skills.name: was
skills.summary: Re-pitches a short message in plain German by adding missing context before simplifying it, while keeping the repo's glossary terms verbatim.
